newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn falls late on 1997 production estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn falls late on 1997 production estimate.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a corn crop production estimate in the fiscal 1998 budget proposed by the Clinton Administration, traders said.

The Clinton budget proposal for the Agriculture Department pegged U.S. corn production for 1997 at 9.625 billion bushels. The U.S. Feed Grains Council early this week pegged U.S. corn production at 9.49 billion bushels.
A sharp break in the soybean market, tied to aggressive fund selling, also hit the corn market, the traders said.
"Wheat and corn just followed suit," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter referring to the collapse in soybeans.
Corn found mild underpinning early on USDA's weekly export sales report.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended January 30 totaled 871,200 tonnes, above expectations for 500,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
Also, USDA early Thursday said U.S. exporters reported a sale of 138,500 tonnes of corn to unknown destinations.
Support under the market came from talk of dry weather in portions of South Africa's maize growing region.
Corn closed 3/4 to 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 3-3/4 at $2.68-3/4.
"There was a little talk about dry weather in South Africa. They could use some rain," Lespinasse said.
Refco Inc sold six million bushels of March and there were an estimated two million bushels sold in the May as spillover selling from the corn options pit, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 46,000 contracts, above the 43,211 traded Wednesday, CBOT said.
In corn options, FIMAT Futures bought 2,000 May $2.70 puts at 7-1/2 to eight cents and Smith Barney bought 1,000 May $2.70 puts at 8-3/4 to nine cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, above the 9,249 traded Wednesday.
